stories.title: Driftwood Capital, Merrimac Ventures Land $145M for Waterfront Hotel in Miami
stories.excerpt: A venture led by Driftwood Capital and Merrimac Ventures has secured a $145 million loan to build a hospitality and retail-focused development along the Miami River. The construction financing from Centennial Bank covers the $350 million Riverside Wharf development, which will feature a 167-room hotel across two nine-story towers at 114 Southwest North River Drive, surrounded by the First Street Drawbridge and Interstate 95, in Downtown Miami. To complete the capital stack, the developers have raised $15 million through the EB-5 program, with the goal of reaching $60 million, according to a representative for the development team. The federal program grants green cards to foreigners, who invest in projects that create or preserve at least 10 full-time jobs. The 200,000-square-foot project will also house a 30,000-square-foot nightclub, a 12,000-square-foot event hall, and 16,000 square feet of restaurant space. The Wharf outdoor bar, which was previously located on the site, will be part of the new offering. Construction is expected to be completed in the fall of 2028, with Moss Construction serving as general contractor. The 1.3-acre Riverside Wharf will rise on land owned by both MV Real Estate Holdings, which remains a partner in the project, and the City of Miami. In 2022, voters approved the sponsor’s request to extend the ground lease by 50 years with the city. The agreement also calls for the construction of a publicly accessible riverwalk and a new seawall. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Driftwood Capital & Merrimac Ventures secured $145M construction loan from Centennial Bank for Miami River project.
Riverside Wharf: 167-room hotel, 30K SF nightclub, 12K SF event hall in Downtown Miami near I-95.
EB-5 program targeting $60M foreign investment for job creation component of $350M total capital stack.
stories.summary: Driftwood Capital and Merrimac Ventures closed $145 million in construction financing from Centennial Bank for the Riverside Wharf development along Miami's river corridor. The mixed-use hospitality project features a 167-room hotel across two nine-story towers plus 30,000 square feet of nightclub and event space in Downtown Miami. Developers are raising $60 million via EB-5 foreign investment program to complete the $350 million capital stack.
stories.impact: This deal signals capital availability for Miami mixed-use development despite broader financing headwinds, but the reliance on EB-5 to fill a $60M gap suggests debt markets remain selective. For multifamily developers in South Florida, watch whether hospitality-heavy projects crowd out residential supply in constrained downtown submarkets, potentially reducing developable land and labor availability in Miami.

stories.title: LMF Commercial Closing Its Doors: Sources
stories.excerpt: LMF Commercial has closed, Commercial Observer has learned. The lender, a Lennar subsidiary, announced the closure internally and started laying off professionals in its New York, Miami, Los Angeles and Las Vegas offices on Oct. 21, several sources said. Lennar officials declined to comment. LMF Commercial was founded in 2013 by Brett Ersoff and John Herman. Prior to founding LMF, the partners led global real estate for UBS. An originator of five- and 10-year, fixed-rate mortgages across multifamily, retail, hotel, self-storage and office assets — with multifamily loans comprising the bulk of its loan portfolio — LMF amassed $14 billion of transactions over the years, with an average loan size of $11.3 million, according to the company’s website. The platform was a mortgage contributor to conduit commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) transactions. LMF Commercial originated a $39 million loan on a Bronx housing portfolio owned by Barry Singer that was transferred to special servicing last year, and was also part of the lending consortium — together with Bank of America and UBS — for Tishman Speyer and Silverstein Properties’ $274 million refinance of the Salmon Tower office building at 11 West 42nd Street in Midtown Manhattan, according to The Real Deal. One source described LMF as “in the process of winding down” and said “they’re no longer making loans.” Another simply said they’d heard Ersoff was “hanging up the cleats.” The reason for the platform closing down has yet to be ascertained but one source noted that originating conduit CMBS loans is becoming increasingly difficult due to the higher-for-longer interest rate environment, “and that was LMF’s business.” The company employs around 50 professionals, according to its LinkedIn page. Its New York office is located at 590 Madison Avenue. Ersoff didn’t return a request for comment. Cathy Cunningham can be reached at ccunningham@commercialobserver.com
bullets: LMF Commercial (Lennar subsidiary) closed abruptly Oct 21, laying off staff in NY, Miami, LA, Las Vegas.
LMF originated $14B in mortgages (avg $11.3M), multifamily-heavy portfolio; operated as CMBS lender since 2013.
$39M Bronx housing loan transferred to special servicing; $274M Tishman Speyer/Silverstein refinance consortium participation affected.
stories.summary: LMF Commercial, a Lennar-backed multifamily and mixed-asset lender founded in 2013, ceased operations and laid off staff across four major offices on October 21. The platform originated $14 billion in mortgages with an average loan size of $11.3 million, with multifamily comprising the bulk of its portfolio and regular CMBS securitization participation. The closure affects existing borrowers including a $39 million Bronx housing portfolio and a $274 million Tishman Speyer/Silverstein consortium refinance.
stories.impact: LMF's sudden closure removes a mid-market multifamily lender and signals tightening capital supply in the $11M loan-size segment—a critical band for most value-add and stabilized asset refinances. Developers relying on fixed-rate, 5–10-year mortgages from secondary lenders face reduced optionality and potential forced renegotiations; affected borrowers in Bronx and Manhattan multifamily portfolios will seek replacement financing in a more constrained market, likely at higher rates and tighter terms.

stories.title: Origin, Mill Creek Teaming Up on 190-Unit Scottsdale Rental Community
stories.excerpt: Origin Investments and its partner, Mill Creek Residential, are planning to build Modera Old Town, a 190-unit multifamily development in an Opportunity Zone in Old Town Scottsdale. Construction on the new community will begin in October, with completion in mid-2029. This new development represents the second venture between Origin and Mill Creek Residential. Origin and Mill Creek’s first development is Modera Higley Commons, a 276-unit community development in Gilbert, Ariz. The new community was completed earlier this year and currently is 87% leased. Modera Old Town will offer amenities including a pool, an outdoor kitchen, poolside cabanas, lounge seating, an outdoor grilling and entertainment area with a fire feature, a resident clubhouse, an entertainment lounge, modern dining and bar space, and a fitness center. Additional offerings include high-end coworking spaces and private conference rooms. For Origin, Modera Old Town represents the final investment in its Opportunity Zone Fund III and its 22nd overall opportunity zone development announced by Origin.  The post Origin, Mill Creek Teaming Up on 190-Unit Scottsdale Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Origin Investments & Mill Creek Residential begin 190-unit Modera Old Town in Opportunity Zone, Old Town Scottsdale.
Construction starts October; delivery mid-2029; co-development team's first project (276-unit Modera Higley Commons, Gilbert) 87% leased.
Final investment in Origin's Opportunity Zone Fund III; 22nd OZ development announced by Origin overall.
stories.summary: Origin Investments and Mill Creek Residential are co-developing Modera Old Town, a 190-unit multifamily community in Old Town Scottsdale within an Opportunity Zone, with construction beginning in October and mid-2029 completion. This marks the second partnership between the two firms; their first joint venture, 276-unit Modera Higley Commons in Gilbert, completed earlier this year and is currently 87% leased. The project represents Origin's final investment from its Opportunity Zone Fund III.
stories.impact: Strong absorption at the pair's Gilbert project (87% leased post-delivery) validates demand in Phoenix metro and signals confidence in Scottsdale submarket fundamentals. The Opportunity Zone structure and co-developer model suggest capital efficiency; however, the mid-2029 delivery is long-duration exposure to Phoenix's competitive supply pipeline—developers should monitor whether 190 units in Old Town will face saturation from other announced projects and whether the OZ tax benefits remain robust through delivery.

stories.title: RCG Ventures Closes Latest Fund Above Target with $515M
stories.excerpt: RCG Ventures, LLC, the vertically integrated real estate investment arm of Argonne Capital Group specializing in multi-tenant retail real estate assets, said Monday it had closed RCG Ventures Fund VIII above target, with $515 million in capital commitments. The fund attracted strong support from a diverse group of new and existing institutional investors. “The successful close of Fund VIII is an endorsement of both our strategy and increasing institutional recognition of multi-tenant retail as an attractive investment opportunity,” said Michael Klump, founder and chairman of RCG and Argonne. “We believe our deep track-record and operating experience, vertically-integrated platform and longstanding relationships position us to identify and execute on compelling opportunities to deliver value for our investors.” The final close builds on recent momentum across RCG’s platform, including its previously announced acquisition of a $1.7-billion multi-tenant retail portfolio from Global Net Lease, Inc., a transaction that more than doubled RCG’s multi-tenant retail footprint. To date, Fund VIII has completed nine acquisitions in key markets across the U.S. and is under contract on an additional five investments. Pictured: Holiday Centre in Monroeville, PA, a recent RCG acquisition. The post RCG Ventures Closes Latest Fund Above Target with $515M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RCG Ventures closed Fund VIII at $515M, above target, for multi-tenant retail acquisitions across U.S.
Fund completed 9 acquisitions; 5 more under contract; platform acquired $1.7B Global Net Lease portfolio (doubled footprint).
Argonne Capital Group's retail-focused fund attracted diverse institutional investor base in 2024 capital markets.
stories.summary: RCG Ventures, the retail investment arm of Argonne Capital Group, closed Fund VIII with $515 million in commitments, exceeding its target. The fund has completed nine acquisitions to date and has five additional investments under contract across key U.S. markets. The strong close follows RCG's acquisition of a $1.7 billion multi-tenant retail portfolio from Global Net Lease, which doubled the firm's retail footprint.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. This signals institutional capital confidence in diversified retail (non-trophy office), which may compete for cap rates and sponsor-quality assets in mixed-use deals; however, retail-focused dry powder does not directly constrain multifamily financing or land availability.

stories.title: BGO Transitions Its Name Back to GreenOak
stories.excerpt: BGO is changing its name yet again. The global real estate investment management and services firm merged with Bentall Kennedy in 2019 to become BentallGreenOak. It then truncated that name to BGO in 2024. Now, it’s switching gears back to GreenOak as part of another massive rebranding effort. Sun Life Financial, the firm’s parent company, announced Monday that its $326 billion institutional asset management platform, SLC Management, will rebrand under that single GreenOak global name. The move brings together the former BGO and its sister firms Crescent Capital, InfraRed Capital Partners, SLC Fixed Income and Advisors Asset Management. The rebranding will be completed within the next year. “The launch of GreenOak reflects the evolution of our business and how we will operate as one integrated platform,” Sonny Kalsi, president and CEO of GreenOak, said in a statement. “While our name may be changing, our focus remains the same: generating strong investment outcomes, delivering exceptional client service, and empowering our people to do their best work.” Sun Life Financial, a Toronto-based international financial services organization with more than $1.6 trillion in assets under management, acquired GreenOak Real Estate in 2018 prior to the 2019 merger with BentallGreenOak to form (eventually) BGO. Its return to the name GreenOak “builds on that history while extending the name beyond its real estate origins,” Sun Life Financial said in its Monday announcement. The then-BGO has been busy on the acquisition front recently. Last month, the firm bought a 100 percent leased, 11-property portfolio of surgery centers across the U.S. from Flagship Healthcare Properties and AEW Capital Management. The purchase price was not disclosed, but the portfolio spans 223,000 square feet across nine markets. bullets: BGO rebrands to GreenOak; Sun Life Financial's $326B SLC Management platform consolidates under single name.
Merger integrates BGO, Crescent Capital, InfraRed, SLC Fixed Income, Advisors Asset Management into one entity.
Organizational rebrand; no new capital or strategy changes announced; focus remains on institutional investment outcomes.
stories.summary: BGO, the real estate investment platform owned by Sun Life Financial, is rebranding to GreenOak as part of a broader consolidation of SLC Management's $326 billion asset platform. The rebrand unifies BGO with sister firms Crescent Capital, InfraRed Capital Partners, SLC Fixed Income, and Advisors Asset Management under a single GreenOak global name. The move is organizational and strategic; no change in investment mandate or capital base was announced.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Rebranding and platform consolidation do not signal material capital deployment shifts or strategy changes; however, developers with existing GreenOak/BGO relationships should clarify counterparty alignment and decision-making authority post-merger.

stories.title: Carrier to Invest $600M in FW Manufacturing Center
stories.excerpt: Carrier Global Corporation plans to invest more than $600 million over the next three years in a new one million square foot advanced manufacturing and engineering center in Fort Worth, Texas. The new state-of-the-art site demonstrates Carrier’s confidence in its growth in this business and furthers Carrier’s commitment to domestic manufacturing as the largest U.S.-headquartered company in its industry. The site will be in Hillwood’s AllianceTexas development. This investment supports Carrier’s expansion of the company’s U.S. manufacturing capacity for advanced thermal management systems, including air- and water-cooled commercial chillers and helps customers meet growing demand for intelligent climate and energy solutions across data centers, healthcare, education, industrial markets and other key verticals. Carrier is expected to begin operations in the facility in 2027. The investment will create 1,500 advanced manufacturing, engineering and other jobs. The post Carrier to Invest $600M in FW Manufacturing Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Carrier Global investing $600M over 3 years in 1M SF advanced manufacturing center in Fort Worth, AllianceTexas.
Facility will create 1,500 jobs in thermal management systems; operations begin 2027; focus on data centers, healthcare, industrial verticals.
Largest U.S.-headquartered company in its industry signals domestic manufacturing commitment and regional employment expansion.
stories.summary: Carrier Global Corporation plans to invest over $600 million over the next three years in a new one million square foot advanced manufacturing and engineering facility in Fort Worth's AllianceTexas development. The project will create 1,500 jobs in advanced manufacturing, engineering, and supporting roles, with operations beginning in 2027. The facility will produce advanced thermal management systems for data centers, healthcare, education, industrial, and other key verticals.
stories.impact: Carrier's 1,500-job facility in Fort Worth (Dallas-Fort Worth metro) will materially increase regional employment and worker in-migration, boosting multifamily rental demand across DFW submarkets, particularly near AllianceTexas in northwest Dallas. Development teams should prioritize land acquisition and underwriting in North Dallas, Irving, and Frisco for build-to-rent or market-rate Class A/B communities targeted at the influx of manufacturing and engineering workers over the 2027–2029 window; housing supply risk is high if development does not begin now.

stories.title: Ascent Acquires 10-Story Dallas Office Tower
stories.excerpt: Ascent Real Estate Advisors has acquired the 10-story Hillcrest Tower in north Dallas. The Dallas Business Journal reports that Ascent purchased the property at 12720 Hillcrest Road from Albany Road Real Estate Partners. The tower, spanning over 168,000 square feet, is 97% leased and has a roster of nearly 50 tenants. CBRE to handle leasing. Newmark Group listed the property for sale in June. Albany Road also owns the 448,000-square-foot Mockingbird Towers at 1341 W. Mockingbird Lane in Dallas, which it bought in 2020. An Ascent-led team reacquired Rambler Park, a 310,943-square-foot, 14-story medical office tower. Ascent also previously owned DFW office buildings such as the roughly 94,00-square foot 5001 Statesman in Irving, the 192,000-square-foot Meadow Central office park in Dallas, and the more than 260,000-square-foot Midway Atriums office complex in Addison. Hillcrest Tower was built in 1982 and renovated in 2022. The post Ascent Acquires 10-Story Dallas Office Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Ascent Real Estate Advisors acquired 10-story Hillcrest Tower in North Dallas; 168K SF, 97% leased, 50 tenants.
Albany Road Real Estate Partners sold property; Newmark listed June 2024; CBRE to handle future leasing.
Ascent team also reacquired 310K SF medical office tower (Rambler Park, 14 stories); established DFW office owner-operator.
stories.summary: Ascent Real Estate Advisors acquired the 10-story Hillcrest Tower in north Dallas from Albany Road Real Estate Partners, a 168,000-square-foot office building 97% leased with nearly 50 tenants. Newmark Group had listed the property for sale in June. Ascent simultaneously reacquired Rambler Park, a 310,943-square-foot medical office tower, signaling an active repositioning strategy in the DFW office market.
stories.impact: Low impact on multifamily development. Ascent's office acquisitions reflect selective institutional capital targeting high-occupancy, diversified-tenant office assets in North Dallas—a signal that trophy office still attracts capital but does not directly affect multifamily land, financing, or demand in DFW. However, the volume of office acquisition activity may indicate land and capital are shifting toward office over multifamily, potentially raising land costs in prime submarkets.

stories.title: Industrial Color Expands to 59K SF at Rudin’s 32 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Industrial Color, a creative production company and network of production studios, has renewed and expanded its lease at Rudin’s Tribeca office property at 32 Avenue of the Americas, Commercial Observer has learned. The company, which has been a tenant at the Tribeca property for over 20 years, signed a 15-year renewal on the 46,638-square-foot space it currently occupies on the building’s entire 22nd floor and part of the 20th floor. The deal included a 12,125-square-foot expansion across part of the 20th floor, which brings Industrial Color’s total office footprint in the building to 58,763 square feet. “There is no stronger endorsement than a tenant of two decades opting to deepen its commitment,” Robert Steinman, senior vice president of office leasing at Rudin, said in a statement. “Renewals like this one speak to the unparalleled value of ownership they can trust for the long term. We’re proud to continue supporting Industrial Color’s growth at 32 Avenue of the Americas for many years to come.” Steinman represented Rudin in-house alongside Craig Panzirer, senior vice president and head of office leasing at the firm. Rudin declined to provide the asking rent for this deal. The average asking rent for office space in Lower Manhattan was $64.88 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers data. Paul Ippolitto and Kyle Wainwright from Newmark represented Industrial Color. Ippolitto and Wainwright did not immediately respond to CO’s requests for comment. Rudin acquired 32 Avenue of the Americas from AT&T in 1999. The property one block south of Canal Street is also home to telecommunications giant Verizon, network and infrastructure services provider Lumen Technologies and flexible workspace provider Industrious. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Industrial Color renewed and expanded lease at Rudin's 32 Avenue of the Americas (Tribeca) for 15 years.
Expansion adds 12,125 SF to existing 46,638 SF; total footprint now 58,763 SF across 20th & 22nd floors.
20-year tenant deepens commitment; Rudin management emphasizes ownership stability and tenant retention in Manhattan office.
stories.summary: Industrial Color, a creative production company and studio network, renewed and expanded its lease at Rudin's Tribeca office building (32 Avenue of the Americas) for 15 years. The company expanded by 12,125 square feet on the 20th floor, bringing its total footprint to 58,763 square feet across the 20th and 22nd floors. Industrial Color has been a tenant at the property for over 20 years, and the renewal reflects confidence in Manhattan office fundamentals and long-term ownership stability.
stories.impact: Minimal impact on multifamily development. This is a positive signal for Midtown Manhattan office and Tribeca stability, but does not affect residential supply, demand, or capital deployment. However, strong office leasing activity in Manhattan may absorb capital and tenant demand that could otherwise support residential conversion or mixed-use development in adjacent neighborhoods.

stories.title: Weidner Adds 341-Unit Rental Asset to Austin Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Weidner Apartment Homes acquired the Solaris House apartments, a 341-unit high-rise apartment complex located in North Austin’s Domain submarket. Brandywine Realty Trust was the seller. JLL represented Brandywine Realty Trust in the sale of the asset. JLL’s Debt Advisory team also arranged acquisition financing for Weidner through Nationwide. The acquisition marks Weidner’s fifth community in the Austin metropolitan area, expanding its local portfolio to 1,560 units. Completed in 2024, Solaris House offers 13 stories of apartment homes, averaging 945 square feet. The property delivers an amenity package featuring a fitness center, coworking lounge, pet spa and outdoor lounge. The signature rooftop pool deck offers private cabanas, grilling stations and a turfed recreation area with sweeping views. JLL’s Capital Markets Investment Sales and Advisory team representing the seller was led by Robert Wooten, Ryan McBride and Robert Arzola. JLL’s Capital Markets Debt Advisory team was led by Tom Wilson, Jayme Nelson and Jake Davidson. The post Weidner Adds 341-Unit Rental Asset to Austin Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Weidner Apartment Homes acquired 341-unit Solaris House high-rise in North Austin Domain submarket from Brandywine Realty Trust.
Solaris House completed 2024, 13 stories, 945 SF average; amenity-rich with rooftop pool, pet spa, coworking.
Acquisition marks Weidner's fifth Austin community; portfolio now 1,560 units; Nationwide financed via JLL debt advisory.
stories.summary: Weidner Apartment Homes acquired Solaris House, a 341-unit, 13-story high-rise apartment complex in North Austin's Domain submarket, from Brandywine Realty Trust. Completed in 2024, the property averages 945 square feet per unit and features premium amenities including rooftop pool, pet spa, coworking lounge, and fitness center. The acquisition expands Weidner's Austin portfolio to five communities and 1,560 total units; Nationwide provided acquisition financing arranged by JLL.
stories.impact: Weidner's acquisition of a stabilized 2024-delivery asset signals strong institutional capital availability for well-amenitied, newer multifamily stock in Austin's Domain submarket—a supply-constrained, high-barrier area. However, Weidner is consolidating existing supply rather than anchoring new development; this suggests premium land for new construction may be scarce or overpriced in Domain. Developers should focus on secondary Austin submarkets (East, South) or identify infill land before domain-focused operators continue roll-ups.

stories.title: Extell to Buy $24M in Air Rights From Episcopal Church for 570 Fifth Avenue Tower
stories.excerpt: Gary Barnett’s Extell Development has nearly secured 87,000 square feet of air rights for its 570 Fifth Avenue office tower project. The rights currently belong to the Church of St. Mary the Virgin, a landmarked Episcopal church at 145 West 46th Street in Midtown’s Times Square neighborhood. A December 2025 purchase and sale agreement between the parties was filed with the New York Supreme Court on Friday for approval, according to PincusCo, and totals $23.93 million. The sale of the air rights has secured approval from the church’s board of trustees, as well as the Protestant Episcopal Church in New York and the diocese’s bishop, Matthew Foster Heyd, according to the filing. It marks the final slice of the Church of Saint Mary the Virgin’s air rights, another 131,000 square feet of which was previously transferred to the Durst Organization’s 114 West 47th Street office tower. No brokers were connected to the sale agreement, according to the filing. The offices of the diocese and the church’s attorney did not respond to requests for comment. The unused development rights will go directly toward developing Extell’s Class A office and retail tower between West 46th and West 47th streets, located one block east of the church. Law firm Simpson Thacher & Bartlett will anchor the office portion of the tower with a 916,000-square-foot lease signed in May, and development partner Ingka Investments will open an 80,000-square-foot Ikea store at the tower’s base. Delivery is expected by the end of 2028. Extell undertook a decades-long buying spree to secure more than a dozen parcels of land for the Fifth Avenue tower, wrapping up with the $175 million acquisition of a corner lot in 2025. Once slated as a 78-story supertall, the project has since downsized. Elsewhere in Midtown, the acquisitions keep coming. bullets: Extell Development purchasing 87K SF air rights from Church of St. Mary the Virgin (145 W 46th St) for $23.93M.
Air rights for 570 Fifth Avenue office tower; church already sold 131K SF air rights to Durst Organization (114 W 47th St).
Purchase agreement filed Dec 2025; approved by church trustees, Protestant Episcopal Church, and diocese; no brokers involved.
stories.summary: Extell Development Company is acquiring 87,000 square feet of air rights from the Church of St. Mary the Virgin, a landmarked Episcopal church at 145 West 46th Street in Midtown Times Square, for $23.93 million. The air rights will be used for Extell's 570 Fifth Avenue office tower project. The church has already transferred 131,000 square feet of air rights to Durst Organization's 114 West 47th Street office tower; this latest sale completes the church's air rights disposition.
stories.impact: Air rights transactions in Midtown Times Square reflect office-focused development and do not directly affect multifamily supply, demand, or capital. However, Extell's $24M air rights purchase signals continued office tower investment in prime Manhattan despite sector headwinds, indicating institutional capital is selective and concentrated in flagship locations and trophy sponsors—competition for capital and land may tighten in secondary multifamily markets as prime office still attracts development capital.
